summary: This clipped ROS 2 documentation page is the Ubuntu installation tutorial for the Webots simulator interface, part of the Simulators section of the Advanced tutorials. It explains that the webots_ros2 package connects ROS 2 with Webots, and gives the lookup order for locating Webots installations. It then covers installing webots_ros2 either from the distributed Debian package or from GitHub sources built with colcon, and launching the webots_ros2_universal_robot multirobot example. Navigation menus and page boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Tutorial for installing the webots_ros2 package on Ubuntu and running the universal robot simulation example in ROS 2.
key_facts: The Installation (Ubuntu) tutorial's goal is to install the webots_ros2 package and run simulation examples on Ubuntu.
The tutorial is rated Advanced level and takes 10 minutes.
The webots_ros2 package provides an interface between ROS 2 and Webots.
The webots_ros2_driver sub-package allows users to start Webots and communicate with it.
If the ROS2_WEBOTS_HOME environment variable is set, ROS 2 uses the Webots in that folder regardless of version.
If WEBOTS_HOME is set and ROS2_WEBOTS_HOME is not, ROS 2 uses the Webots in that folder regardless of version.
Without these variables, webots_ros2 looks in /usr/local/webots and /snap/webots/current/usr/share/webots for a compatible version.
If Webots cannot be found, webots_ros2 offers a window for automatic installation of the latest compatible version.
The distributed package is installed with sudo apt-get install ros-rolling-webots-ros2.
Installing from sources involves creating ~/ros2_ws/src, cloning https://github.com/cyberbotics/webots_ros2.git with submodules, installing dependencies with rosdep, and running colcon build.
The example is launched with ros2 launch webots_ros2_universal_robot multirobot_launch.py.
The example launch uses export WEBOTS_HOME=/usr/local/webots to select a specific Webots installation.
The tutorial's prerequisites recommend the beginner tutorials Creating a workspace and Creating a package.
The page is copyright 2023, GrantLi, and was built with Sphinx.
